question: Refer to the exhibit. Which VLANs are capable to be assigned on vPC interfaces?
context:
switch# show vpc brief
Legend:
        (*) - local vPC is down, forwarding via vPC peer-link

vPC domain id                  : 10
Peer status                    : peer adjacency formed ok
vPC keep-alive status          : peer is alive
Configuration consistency status : success
Type-2 consistency status      : success
vPC role                       : primary
Number of vPCs configured      : 1
Peer Gateway                   : Enabled
Dual-active exluded VLANs      : -

vPC Peer-link status
---------------------------------------------------------------
id   Port   Status   Active vlans
--   ----   ------   --------------------------------------------------
1    Po20   up       100-105

vPC status
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
id   Port   Status   Consistency  Reason                Active vlans
--   ----   ------   -----------  --------------------  -----------
7    Po7    up       success      success               100-104
8    Po8    up       success      success               100-102
9    Po9    up       success      success               100-103
theory: A vPC member port can only carry VLANs that are also allowed across the vPC peer link, because the peer link is what synchronizes MAC/IGMP state and carries traffic for orphan ports on those VLANs. The peer-link's active VLAN range (100-105 in the "show vpc brief" output) is therefore the superset that bounds what any individual vPC (Po7, Po8, Po9) is allowed to carry, even though each specific vPC shows a narrower currently-active subset. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC Peer Link and VLAN Consistency)
